queryLog.query: barber cuts, beard trims, and father-son haircut appointments service marketing website homepage book CTA landing page website inspiration
book CTA homepage with trust proof, service or product menu, and local customer decision path website
queryLog.notes: Collected as a 6-result retry plus a 2-result retry after an 8-result chunk timed out.

queryLog.query: premium credible owner-led service business landing page website
family booking path service duration comparison masculine visual language without cliche responsive mobile-first homepage website not dashboard not app

rawCandidates.selectionReason: Booking-first hero model for a fast service decision.
Venue-detail page pattern for service proof and booking placement.
Service rows map cleanly to cut, beard trim, and father-son appointment comparison.
Grooming category tone reference without barber-shop cliche.
Compact menu state shows how to keep mobile navigation light.
Menu overlay offers a reference for light utility navigation.
Appointment duration and date/time selection map well to barber services.
Dark scheduling card gives a controlled masculine contrast without fake barbershop nostalgia.
Group/guest count pattern is useful for parent-child appointment branching.
Sparse editorial tone reference for premium-but-plain service presentation.
Business-provider page gives useful image cluster and benefit-copy warning patterns.
Provider-side booking benefit page is useful for explaining easy online booking, but not for customer-visible proof.
Generic service-card page is useful as an anti-reference.
Dark portfolio treatment is useful as a cliche warning for masculine visuals.
Admin-side booking setup is useful as an anti-reference for customer-facing pages.
Group booking modal helps stress family-visit branching and price/guest clarity.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Make the first action a booking decision for cut, beard, or father-son appointment.
Lead with fast appointment choice, then explain service differences below.
Use a calm booking hero with one strong horizontal action area.
Collapse booking controls into large mobile rows with clear service labels.

bannedUses: Do not copy Fresha's beauty category language, pastel identity, appointment counts, or marketplace promise.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Show process and service clarity as proof when reviews or ratings are not source-backed.
Each service row should have a book action so visitors do not hunt for the next step.
Different service rows can route to different booking durations or enquiry prompts.
Service rows need scannable labels, durations, and button names for keyboard and touch users.

bannedUses: Do not invent prices, ratings, photos, staff names, or service claims from the reference.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A grooming-object still life can replace fake shop interiors if actual photos are absent.
Use deeper navy/cream accents carefully instead of generic black-and-gold barber cliche.
Flat product staging can create polish without heavy shadows.
Use crisp geometry and simple controls rather than ornate vintage motifs.

bannedUses: Do not copy Dollar Shave Club products, packaging, subscription language, or consumer-goods positioning.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Let the visitor choose service duration before date/time when that lowers booking hesitation.
Duration, selected date, unavailable slot, and repeated-family booking states must be explicit.
Use local time, duration, and booking labels that match the Cork context.
Date/time selectors need stable tokenized sizes so rows do not shift across devices.

bannedUses: Do not expose raw scheduling-app complexity, calendar overlays, or internal account UI.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use a compact, confident type rhythm instead of exaggerated macho display type.
Write like a clear local operator: direct service names, no swagger copy.
A dark booking block can anchor the page without making the whole site gloomy.
Pair a calendar/list region with a plain next action and escape route.

bannedUses: Do not copy Braintrust branding, black calendar visuals wholesale, or consultation marketplace language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Separate parent-child booking from standard cut and beard trim to reduce uncertainty.
Use enough breathing room around family/party controls so booking does not feel crowded.
Parent-child booking can use a simple party selector or grouped appointment prompt.
Expose service names and duration rules in visible and agent-readable metadata.

bannedUses: Do not copy travel/experience pricing, guest labels, or Airbnb brand patterns.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: If used, movement should be subtle: menu reveal, service selection, or booking step transition.
A strong no-photo graphic can carry atmosphere without pretending to show the shop.
Use utility icons only where they clarify service, time, location, or family visit.
Avoid full-bleed heavy video or photo assets until real shop media exists.

bannedUses: Do not use meditation/wellness positioning, subscription copy, or unapproved lifestyle photography.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Mobile menus need clear labels and reachable touch targets.
Utility navigation must not expose unready claims, unsupported booking modes, or fake business details.
Keep proof areas absent or process-based until real reviews, photos, and shop details are approved.
The primary booking action should remain available when menus are open.

bannedUses: Do not copy account menu items, marketplace links, language selector, or app-download CTA.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Generic AI service-card layout would make the barber page feel template-made.
Dark agency portfolio styling is the wrong kind of masculine and would become a cliche.
Admin setup UI is not a customer-facing barber website reference.
Provider growth claims and marketplace revenue proof cannot be reused for a local barber fixture.

remixDirection.summary: A fast-booking barber page with crisp service comparison, a restrained grooming-object visual system, explicit family-visit branching, and a mobile-first booking path.
selectedMoves: Fresha-style booking/search discipline, rebuilt around cut, beard, and father-son visit choices.
Fresha service-row logic for duration comparison and per-service CTAs.
Dollar Shave Club grooming-object restraint without subscription or product-store positioning.
Cal.com duration selector logic for appointment length clarity.
Airbnb group selector logic adapted to parent-child appointment grouping.
explicitRejects: No fake shop photos, ratings, reviews, barber names, heritage story, or masculine cliche palette.
No marketplace appointment counts, provider-growth claims, or admin UI.
No exact layout copy from any shortlisted screen.
